guideposts.label: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 21 of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: It’s the end of the road. After over 3,000 kilometres of racing, with some 5,000 metres of elevation gain, from Monaco, home to the Salida Official of La Vuelta 26 three weeks ago, the peloton are in Granada for the final stage. It will be an exilarating finale, with a punchy circuit around the iconic Alhambra to cap off this 81st edition. The times for the general classification will be neutralis

guideposts.label: A historic finale
guideposts.detail: In its 81st edition, La Vuelta finishes in Granada for the first time. Madrid is the venue that has crowned the final winners on most occasions (55), ahead of Bilbao (13), San Sebastián (6), Santiago de Compostela (3), and then Miranda de Ebro, Salamanca and Jerez de la Frontera (1 each). Granada was a stage town already in the first La Vuelta (1935), and it hosted the Gran Salida in 2005 and 2008

guideposts.label: Remembering the Galera brothers
guideposts.detail: Today’s start from Carrefour Granada sees the riders roll from Armilla, the hometown of the Galera brothers. Born in 1940, Joaquin Galera won a stage of the Tour de France in 1965 and passed away last year. His younger brother Manuel was born in 1943 and died after a crash during the 1972 edition of the Vuelta a Andalucia. The same year, the Memorial Manuel Galera was celebrated for the first time

guideposts.label: La Roja
guideposts.detail: The all-out action en route to Collado del Alguacil all but settled the overall battle. Enric Mas (Movistar) is set to become the 64th different overall winner of La Vuelta. He will be the 25th different Spanish winner of La Vuelta, the first since Alberto Contador in 2014.It will also be the fifth La Vuelta overall victory in the history of team Movistar after the successes of Pedro Delgado (1989

guideposts.label: Green jersey
guideposts.detail: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) is set to become the 13th Belgian winner of the points standings of La Vuelta, the second this century after Greg Van Avermaet in 2008. It will be his second victory in a Grand Tour standings, after the points classification of the Tour de France 2022. guideposts.label: Polka dot jersey
guideposts.detail: Despite Wout van Aert’s assault yesterday, Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) is set to become the fifth Colombian winner of the mountains standings of La Vuelta after Luis Herrera (1987, 1991), Oscar de Jesus Vargas (1989), Martin Farfan (1990) and Felix Cardenas (2003, 2004). guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: Decathlon CMA CGM are set to win the team standings. XDS Astana are 39’01’’ behind the French team while Bahrain Victorious trail by 57’36’’.

guideposts.label: La Vuelta 27 will start from Galicia
guideposts.detail: The Oficial Salida of the 82nd edition of La Vuelta will be set in Galicia, as announced before today’s stage by Javier Guillén, General Director of La Vuelta, and and Marcos Gómez, Commissioner of the Jacobean Holy Year. guideposts.detail: At the start, the organisers and the peloton celebrate five riders who are completing their final Grand Tour before retiring: - Steven Kruiswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) - David de la Cruz (Pinarello Q36.5) - Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious) - Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) - Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH)

guideposts.label: 24 kilometres in the first hour
guideposts.detail: After the early celebrations, the bunch have accelerated now.

guideposts.detail: Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) will finish 4th overall after his many attacks en route to the Collado del Alguacil: “Yesterday was a good day for us. We knew we had a lot to play for, and although in the end it didn’t go quite as we’d hoped, we rode a fairly aggressive race, with those of us in contention for the podium staying in the mix. guideposts.detail: The winner of stage 8 in Xeraco, Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) hopes to be in the mix today: “It’s always special. For a start, it’s really great to finish a Grand Tour, especially when you’ve had some success in it. I’m really pleased to have won. guideposts.label: The race is in Granada
guideposts.detail: The riders will pass the finish line a first time with 41.8 km to go. The road will rise immediately afterwards to climb to the Alhambra. The average speed after 2 hours: 32.3 km/h.

guideposts.label: First time at the finish line
guideposts.detail: 41.8km to go.

guideposts.label: Tronchon attacks
guideposts.detail: The first move of the day comes 28 kilometres from the line. He's followed by a dozen riders, starting with Johannessen and Brennan. Then it's Paret-Peintre, Fisher-Black...

guideposts.label: 2 laps to go
guideposts.detail: Behind the leaders, the bunch has split in two parts. Uno-X Mobility drive the first peloton less than 10 seconds behind the leaders.

guideposts.label: The first chase group catch the leaders
guideposts.detail: Movistar set the pace behind them.

guideposts.label: Bilbao attacks, Van Aert is dropped!
guideposts.detail: 9 kilometres to go...

guideposts.label: Laurance counter-attacks
guideposts.detail: Over the top, Axel Laurance (Netcompany Ineos) passes Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious). Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United) struggle to keep up with the pace set by Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) in pursuit.

guideposts.label: Laurance is caught by a small group
guideposts.detail: There are 11 riders at the frontwith 6.5 km to go.

guideposts.label: Tobias Johannessen wins stage 21 of La Vuelta 26!
guideposts.detail: The Norwegian takes his first Grand Tour stage ahead of Romele!
